searchDocs.title: Function​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Function { client: { InvokeServer: (...any) → (...any), OnClientInvoke: (...any) → (...any) } server: { InvokeClient: ( Player , ...any ) → (...any), OnServerInvoke: ( Player , ...any ) → (...any) } }

searchDocs.title: Installation
searchDocs.content: Installation TypedRemote is published through Wally, you may access it through here:https://wally.run/package/downrest/typedremote

searchDocs.title: Usage
searchDocs.content: Usage TypedRemote is a simple library for declaratively handling remote instances. Similar to libraries likeNet, but with the additional support for type functions. Hooray for verbose parameters / returns! info This is by no means, an "all-in-one" networking library. It manages remotes, but doesn't do extra work like compression, type validation, and batching. -- server local Event = TypedRemote.newReliableEvent("Event") :: TypedRemote.ToServerEvent<(fah: string, foo: boolean) -> ()> Event.server.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player: Player, fah: string, foo: boolean) -- do something end) -- client -- TypeError: Expected this [3.14] to be 'boolean', but got 'number' Event.client:FireServer("foo", 3.14)

searchDocs.title: Event​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Event { client: { FireServer: () → (), OnClientEvent: { Connect: ( self: any, callback: (...any) → () ) → (), ConnectParallel: ( self: any, callback: (...any) → () ) → (), Once: ( self: any, callback: (...any) → () ) → () } }} server: { FireClient: () → (), OnServerEvent: { Connect: ( self: any, callback: (...any) → () ) → (), ConnectParallel: ( self: any, callback: (...any) → () ) → (), Once: ( self: any, callback: (...any) → () ) → () } }} }

searchDocs.title: No more manual management of remote instances​
searchDocs.content: This means you don't have to manually manage remote instances anymore. Yes, you have now displaced the work from managing remotes in Explorer to defining remotes through code.  You may already find this convenient to manage (no more worrying about how to organize remotes in Explorer), but in case you don't, it's a "worthy sacrifice" for the further benefits that it brings (keep reading).

searchDocs.title: Single access point for remotes​
searchDocs.content: With manual remotes, it's each script's job to both know the remote's path and directly access said remote.  local Event1 = ReplicatedStorage...   If you wanted to merely change where this remote instance would be placed, you'd have to update every single line accessing that remote. With an shared Event.luau, all point to that same module, meaning you can just modify the path without having to change lines from scripts.  -- want to change what Event1 points to? go ahead, no need to change me :3 local Event1 = Event.Event1

searchDocs.title: Easy onboarding for networking libraries​
searchDocs.content: Shared Event.luau modules are standard practice when using networking libraries.  Why? Because it's a single access point for managing remotes. Most networking libraries (including TypedRemote, wink wink) either support or force typechecking, and you'd just store the type into that single access point.  export type EventType = (param1: string, param2: boolean) -> () -- best experienced in --!strict Event.Event1 = TypedRemote.newReliableEvent("Event1") :: TypedRemote.ToServerEvent<EventType>

searchDocs.title: newReliableEvent​
searchDocs.content: </> TypedRemote.newReliableEvent( remoteName: string-- Name for Event (reliable) ) → Event<toClientSignature,toServerSignature>-- Event (reliable) object Creates an Event (reliable) object, automatically creating a RemoteEvent instance named remoteName. -- server local ReliableEvent = TypedRemote.newReliableEvent("ReliableEvent") :: TypedRemote.ToServerEvent<(text: string) -> ()> ReliableEvent.server.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player: Player, text: string) foo(text) end) -- client ReliableEvent.client:FireServer("foo")

searchDocs.title: wrapReliableEvent​
searchDocs.content: </> TypedRemote.wrapReliableEvent( remoteEvent: RemoteEvent -- RemoteEvent instance for Event (reliable) object ) → Event<toClientSignature,toServerSignature>-- Event (reliable) object Creates an Event (reliable) object, using a passed RemoteEvent instance, remoteEvent. -- server local ReliableEvent = TypedRemote.wrapReliableEvent(Instance.new("RemoteEvent")) :: TypedRemote.ToServerEvent<(text: string) -> ()> ReliableEvent.server.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player: Player, text: string) foo(text) end) -- client ReliableEvent.client:FireServer("foo")

searchDocs.title: newFunction​
searchDocs.content: </> TypedRemote.newFunction( remoteFunctionName: string-- Name for Function object ) → Function<fromClientSignature,fromServerSignature>-- Function object Creates an Function object, automatically creating a RemoteFunction instance named remoteFunctionName. -- server local Function = TypedRemote.newFunction("Function") :: TypedRemote.FromServerFunction<(text: string) -> (string)> Function.server.OnServerInvoke = function(player: Player, text: string): string return text end -- client local text: string = Function.client:InvokeServer("foo")
